Hi Christine —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I wanted to put a short note that captures the two threads you asked about: (1) the technical levers we recommend for reducing per-token cost (batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization options) and (2) the commercial structure that maps to those savings (credits / commitment tiers / pilot pricing). I attached a short one-pager (Redwood_Optimize_Pricing_Overview.pdf) that summarizes the offer and a few example scenarios.

Quick asks so we can finalize a tailored proposal:
- Can you confirm expected monthly token volume (avg and 95th pct) and any hard latency SLOs for inference (p50/p95)? You mentioned 1M/day as a ballpark — is that production traffic or pilot?
- Do you need private deployment (VPC/on-prem) or is hosted API acceptable for the pilot?
- Any procurement constraints (PO lead time, required contract clauses) we should be aware of?

High level — what we recommend technically for the workload you described:
- Quantization: start with int8 quantization of the model for batch-serving (expected 35–50% cost reduction vs float16); consider 4-bit only if you validate quality on your prompts (we can share an eval harness).
- Batching: continuous-batching with an adaptive max latency of ~40ms for interactive flows; for background bulk generation use larger batch windows for better throughput.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts and stable context (customer messages + identities) — this often gives ~15–25% token savings.

If it's helpful I can loop in Karthik (our inference optimization lead) to include a short savings estimate for your volumes. Would you be available for a 30-min call Thursday afternoon?

Best,

Christine / Stephanie —

Looping in a few technical details so you have concrete numbers for the pilot plan. Summary recommendations based on volume / latency constraints you shared:

1) Quantization strategy
- Start with int8 (post-training dynamic quantization). For many modern open LLMs this preserves quality for your prompt types and gives ~35–45% reduction in GPU memory and per-token compute.
- If you want further upside, run a small A/B eval (we can run 1k prompt pairs) to validate int4; expect additional ~20% compute reduction but higher risk of subtle generation drift.

2) Batching and latency
- Use adaptive continuous batching with a max batch wait of 25–40ms for interactive endpoints to stay within p95=300ms — we assume a single-token generation latency of ~10–15ms on our chosen hardware (NVIDIA H100-class); larger models will increase that baseline.
- For background jobs, configure a large-batch path (batch window 200–500ms) to maximize throughput.

3) Caching (KV / prefix)
- If a portion of the prompts reuse a stable context (e.g., patient intake template, common clinical prompts), enable prefix caching at the route level. Typical token savings 10–25% depending on repetition.

4) Mixed deployment suggestion
- Pilot on Hosted API with an Optimize toolkit credit bundle (see Stephanie's doc). If production requires VPC, move to Redwood Dedicated with reserved capacity and autoscale burst; this gives predictable latency and unit economics.

Preliminary cost-savings example (rough):
- Baseline (float16, no cache): $X per 1M tokens/day
- With int8 + adaptive batching + prefix cache: ~45% lower unit cost (estimate)

I've attached a quick savings estimate CSV that maps your 1M/day scenario across commit tiers. Happy to refine once we have the exact model family and expected prompt mix.
